Problem: Current backlog row is too coarse and treats mock creation mainly as historical weighting + generation.
Solution: Extend F-051 into a versioned exam-blueprint registry plus constrained paper assembly and fidelity validation.
Implementation Notes: Use Board→Qualification→Subject→CurriculumVersion→PaperCode→PaperType/Variant→BlueprintVersion; preserve official-vs-inferred rule provenance; select validated Question/QuestionPart/AssessmentBlock candidates; validate hard constraints separately from soft objectives; render interactive/PDF output; feed attempts into Learning Evidence.
Requirements: Versioned blueprint; validated question bank; assessment blocks; solver strategy; fidelity report; provenance; evidence integration.
Research Linkage: Exam authenticity, assessment validity, learning evidence
Validation Metric: Blueprint fidelity by component + hard-constraint pass rate + generation validity
Agent Notes: Canonical feature retained; see MOCK_EXAM_GENERATOR_ARCHITECTURE.md and ADR-018.

Problem: Paper construction rules drift when official versions or historical corpus analytics change.
Solution: Persist versioned, scoped blueprint records with provenance and validation state.
Implementation Notes: Identity = Board+Qualification+Subject+CurriculumVersion+PaperCode+PaperType/Variant+BlueprintVersion; store direct board rules separately from inferred historical analytics.
Requirements: Blueprint repository; versioning; provenance; activation/validation state.
Research Linkage: Exam structure inference must remain auditable
Agent Notes: New capability; do not duplicate F-051. IDs avoid collision with existing F-164…F-170 subject-architecture rows.

Problem: Question parts sharing a stem/data/diagram can become invalid if independently shuffled or substituted.
Solution: Introduce AssessmentBlock/QuestionGroup semantics for shared context and atomic selection.
Implementation Notes: Persist shared stimulus/data/diagram/stem relationships and select blocks when required; retain QuestionPart identity underneath.
Requirements: Block integrity validation; ordering constraints; block-aware solver candidates.
Validation Metric: Zero invalid shared-context assemblies + block integrity test coverage

Problem: A mock can look realistic while violating marks, structure, AO mix or calculator/internal-choice rules.
Solution: Produce component-level machine-readable fidelity reports and enforce hard-constraint gates.
Implementation Notes: Validate exact and percentage dimensions; never let a scalar score hide a hard failure; retain deviation reasons and blueprint version.
Requirements: Hard-constraint pass rate; component fidelity report; reproducible validation.

Problem: Exam-authentic mocks and diagnostic mocks need different trade-offs between blueprint fidelity and learner targeting.
Solution: Add explicit Exam Simulation and Adaptive Diagnostic Mock policies; use learner evidence only within valid blueprint constraints.
Implementation Notes: Signals: SpecificationPoint mastery/evidence, misconceptions, fluency gaps, exposure/reuse, exam date, teacher priorities; mandatory structure remains hard constraints.
Requirements: Policy/version registry; candidate weighting; reproducibility; evidence linkage.
Validation Metric: Learning-gain and blueprint-validity evaluation; no hard-rule violations
Agent Notes: New capability; distinct from Problem Buster.

Problem: Naive numeric mutation or LLM generation can silently change difficulty, answer ranges, units or mark schemes.
Solution: Generate variants only through a gated source→generation→deterministic/domain validation→mark-scheme validation→review→servable pipeline.
Implementation Notes: Retain source lineage, model/provider/prompt metadata, validation state and rejection reasons; never make generated content canonical board truth.
Requirements: Numerical/domain/unit checks; answer and mark-scheme alignment; human review where required.
Validation Metric: Validated-variant pass rate + zero unvalidated learner serves
Agent Notes: Later capability; high-risk and not Cycle 1.

Problem: Generated mocks can be useful to test whether predicted performance matches actual performance, but current prediction UI must not fabricate grades.
Solution: Create a research/evaluation pipeline comparing prediction vs mock outcomes at overall, SpecificationPoint and question levels.
Implementation Notes: Store model/version, prediction timestamp, eligible population, mock blueprint/version, outcome window and calibration/error metrics; UI remains explicit not-implemented until validated.
Requirements: Calibration; prediction error; readiness classification; leakage controls; outcome windows.
Validation Metric: Calibration error + discrimination + later assessment correlation
Agent Notes: Future research feature; not a fake predicted-grade card.
